$comment: Good practices round 2, 4 and 6 install when missing. `check` says how to tell whether it is present; `install` is the text or change to propose; `class` follows doctor-policy.md. A practice that conflicts with something the user configured on purpose is raised, not installed.

practices.title: Files written for agents are in English
practices.why: Fewer tokens than the same text in most other languages, and it matches the language of agent tooling and skill descriptions.
practices.check: The user-level instruction file states which language agent-facing files use; agent-facing files are in English (discover.mjs reports a language per doc).
practices.install: Files written for agents (instruction files, rules, skills, specs, plans, memory) are in English: fewer tokens, and it matches the tooling. Talk to the user in their language.
practices.followUp: Translate existing agent-facing files (class translate-agent, queued in doctor mode, drafted in <ws>/drafts/).

practices.title: A short skills index in the instruction file
practices.why: Skills only help when the agent reaches for them; an index that says when to use each one makes them fire without being named.
practices.check: The user-level instruction file has a skills section that matches what is installed.
practices.install: See round 6, 'Skills index'. Generated from the installed skills, at most about ten lines.

practices.title: The agent is told to query the knowledge graph
practices.why: A graph that is built and never queried costs build time and gives nothing.
practices.check: graphify-out/ exists and an instruction file tells the agent when to query it.

practices.title: Fresh evidence before claiming done
practices.why: The most common agent failure is reporting success from what should have happened.
practices.check: An instruction or an installed skill requires running the check before saying the work is done.
practices.install: Before saying work is done, run the check that proves it (tests, build, the command, a re-read of the file) in this turn and report what it showed, including what you could not check.

practices.title: Prefer an official CLI over an MCP server for the same service
practices.why: A CLI costs nothing until used; an MCP server adds its tool definitions to every session.
practices.check: For every MCP server whose service has an official CLI, the CLI is installed and logged in, and an instruction file says to prefer it.
practices.install: See round 7, "CLI-first instruction". Generated from the CLIs actually installed.

practices.title: MCP servers at project level unless needed everywhere
practices.why: A user-level server loads its tool definitions into every session of every project; most are needed by one or two projects.
practices.check: Every user-level MCP server is used in nearly every conversation regardless of project; the rest live in the projects that need them.
practices.install: See round 7, "MCP policy". Present the options per server; never move one without the user's choice.

practices.title: No commit, push, PR or merge without an explicit ask
practices.why: Outward-facing and hard to undo; agents otherwise treat them as the natural end of a task.
practices.check: An instruction or permission rule covers commit, push, PR and merge.
practices.install: Never commit, push, open a pull request or merge unless the user asked for that step in this session. Never force-push or rewrite published history.

practices.title: One branch and worktree per concurrent session
practices.why: Two sessions in one working directory overwrite each other's changes and commit each other's work.
practices.check: An instruction covers branch naming and worktrees for parallel sessions, or the project defines its own protocol.
practices.install: Each concurrent session works on its own branch in its own worktree, named <type>/<task-slug>-<YYYYMMDD>. Check the current branch before every commit.

practices.title: Test hooks and gates in a throwaway repo
practices.why: Testing a gate by mutating the working repo (reset, probe commits) destroys work.
practices.check: An instruction says how to test git hooks.
practices.install: Never test a git hook or gate by mutating the working repo. Use a throwaway `git init` fixture in a temp dir.

practices.title: Secrets never printed, never committed
practices.why: Anything printed reaches the transcript; anything committed reaches every clone.
practices.check: An instruction covers masking secrets in output; the project ignores .env* and key files; ideally a pre-commit secret scan exists.
practices.install: Never print a secret, token or key, even partially beyond the first 4 characters. Never add credential files to git.

practices.title: A docs index the instruction file points to
practices.why: With more than about ten docs, the agent cannot tell which one answers the question without reading them all.
practices.check: A file lists each doc with what it answers and when to read it, and an instruction file points to it.
practices.install: One line per doc: path, the question it answers, when to read it. Point to it from the project instruction file.

practices.title: Third-party instructions update on notice, not silently
practices.why: An auto-updating plugin or skill from someone else's branch runs their next push in your sessions with your permissions.
practices.check: Marketplaces and skill sources are pinned or set to notify.
practices.install: Pin the version, or switch the source to notify-then-update.
